import re
lines=open('/home/usain/Dynamic-Agentic-Engineering-OS/docs/DECISION_REGISTER.md',encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')
heads=[]
for i,l in enumerate(lines):
    m=re.match(r'^### (DEC-(\d+))\b(.*)',l)
    if m: heads.append((int(m.group(2)),i))
# sections
secs=[(i,l) for i,l in enumerate(lines) if l.startswith('## ')]
import bisect
# compute entry spans (until next ### or ## heading)
starts=sorted([i for _,i in heads]+[i for i,_ in secs])
out=[]
for n,i in heads:
    j=bisect.bisect_right(starts,i)
    end=starts[j] if j<len(starts) else len(lines)
    body='\n'.join(lines[i:end])
    # section
    k=bisect.bisect_right([s for s,_ in secs],i)-1
    sec=secs[k][1] if k>=0 else ''
    out.append((n,i+1,end,len(body),sec[:90]))
import json
json.dump(out,open('/tmp/gov-os-assessment-C/entries.json','w'))
sizes=[o[3] for o in out]
print(len(out),'entries; median size',sorted(sizes)[len(sizes)//2],'max',max(sizes))
for o in out:
    if o[0] in (100,200,300,400,500,600,700,800,817): print(o)
EOF

task: Lens C of the October 2026 independent assessment. Sample at least 60 register decisions across its whole span, classify them, trace each one to where it landed, and judge two things: whether behaviour corrections reach agents through the skills and briefs, and whether specification decisions reach the Contract and the specifications.
status: DONE
work_completed: I sampled 63 decisions, every 13th id from DEC-010 to DEC-816, with the start drawn by `random.Random(20261019)`. They split into 26 specification, 19 process, 9 owner policy, 7 behaviour correction and 2 superseded, each traced to file and line. 55 reached the right place, 4 reached it in part (DEC-309, DEC-673, DEC-738, DEC-803), 3 did not (DEC-062, DEC-140, DEC-361), and 1 is not yet due (DEC-816). I also traced where all 813 entries are cited, by era and by channel. The report has 10 findings, each with the two classification lines and a severity, and 8 recommendations. I read it once more from the file and corrected the line numbers and quotes my checks showed were stale.
files_changed: Only the report, newly created at `/home/usain/Dynamic-Agentic-Engineering-OS/.gov-runtime/scratch/assessment/2026-10/C-decisions-to-spec.md`, plus my own scratch folder `/tmp/gov-os-assessment-C/` (17 scripts and their saved output). No file, index, branch, ref or worktree of the repository was changed.
evidence: Read-only git commands in the main repository (show, log, diff --cached, grep, ls-files, check-ignore, merge-base --is-ancestor), and `python3 -I` scripts in `/tmp/gov-os-assessment-C/` that import no repository code. The Contract comparison prints "differences: 3" for both 4.1 and 4.2 (providers of CAP-28, CAP-28.a and CAP-30.e). Of the 99 Wave 2 entries, 16 are in the prompt or project briefs, 9 more only in WBS §0, 52 only in the scratch briefs, and none in the kernel. Only 8 of 69 residual commits carry `Task: decision-record`. The earlier entry does not show 134 of the 138 relations recorded on later entries. 40 entries still read PROPOSED, though all were settled later.
tests: None run. I ran no gov or tk command, no suite, no clone, no index build and no launch, so the resource gate never applied and the embedding service was not used.
discoveries: No behaviour correction has reached the kernel since 2026-10-09 (`9ca2c9cb`), and no Wave 2 entry is cited there. Wave 2's working rules live mostly in scratch briefs that git ignores; those briefs carry them consistently (44 of 45 carry DEC-731 and DEC-732). The committed prompt still shows the trailing `&` launch form that DEC-731 replaced, and lacks DEC-732 and DEC-733. The Contract's text has taken no decision since DEC-255 (2026-10-04). Its two forms differ on three provider lists, and 4.2 sits on the held `w2/W2-49` while W2-02 builds to 4.2 on a branch that holds 4.1. The register does not mark later supersessions, corrections or suspensions (for example DEC-709) on the earlier entry. W2-11's fixed list leaves out DEC-802, DEC-803 and DEC-809. API-0002 points to a command file that does not exist.
risks: An orchestrator started from a fresh clone, a cleaned scratch folder, or a repository that adopts the kernel (EXAMIN, UPIM, ASMO) follows the committed prompt and the Wave 1 kernel text. It would hit refused launches, verification run against the wrong tree, and refused closes at the probe gate. Later steps catch each of these; none fails open or loses work. W2-28 and W2-30 would read Contract 4.1 if they start before W2-49 merges. Because statuses are not updated, a replaced rule can still reach an agent's context.
lessons: A decision that lands nowhere an agent reads is not followed: DEC-140 was followed in 8 of 69 cases. A one-time promotion into the kernel (DEC-537) fixes one moment, not the flow, and the gap reopens; what is needed is a landing rule that a check enforces, not a list.
proposed_decisions: None of these is a round; the report gives the DEC-809 classification line.
- R-1: the owner edits prompt §4 and A5 to carry DEC-731 as DEC-799 left it, DEC-732, DEC-733, DEC-738 item 2 and DEC-673.
- R-2: commit a Wave 2 common lead brief made from `A5-early-template.md`.
- R-3: turn W2-11's KPI into a rule and give W2-55 a "lands in" tag, both riding along under DEC-802, with W2-11's close as an entry criterion under DEC-803.
- R-4: align the Contract's two forms in W2-49's resume, and make W2-49's merge an entry criterion of W2-28 and W2-30.
- R-5: mark the 14 relations that change what stands, and fix the register header.
- R-6: a kernel auditor brief template that carries DEC-430; the owner applies or withdraws DEC-062 and DEC-140.
- R-7: a Wave 3 row for API-0002.
- R-8: one canonical text for the judgement rules.
unresolved: I did not run `gov context`, so its output was not measured. Four calls were refused and none was retried. Before the fourth refusal, three whole-repository `git grep -l` searches and one over two project subfolders ran. They printed file names only, and the report's limits disclose this. The class given to each decision is my judgement. The claude.ai Gmail and Google Calendar connectors need authorisation in the claude.ai connector settings and are unavailable until then; I did not use them.
recommended_next_action: The owner makes R-1's prompt edit, one commit and no round, before the next lead brief is written, and folds R-3's KPI change into W2-11 before it starts. The orchestrator copies the report byte for byte to `docs/assessment/2026-10/C-decisions-to-spec.md`.
